thread:
Sophie: hey team — saw a weird p99 tail last night after we bumped default max_tokens for the chat endpoint. throughput steady but tail jumps when the mix includes a few long sequences (>1600). any ideas?

Raj: can you paste the profiler trace? my gut says kernel fallback + KV cache churn. when seq crosses ~2048 we hit a slower attention kernel on some V100/older hw.

Sophie: attaching a tiny trace snippet from the sampler run:
```
seq=1800: kernel=AUTO->ATTN_FALLBACK, kernel_switch_ms=42, kv_miss=3, batch_size=6
seq=512: kernel=OPTIMIZED, kernel_ms=6
```

Matt: oh nice, that 42ms is the killer. also noticed prefix cache eviction spikes in the same window — many long requests cause small microbatches and repeated KV rebuilds.

Linh: confirmed on staging: when request length > 1500 we see less batching (requests wait for token generation) so effective microbatch sizes drop to 1-2, then kernel overhead dominates.

Raj: two levers: 1) prevent very long requests from entering the low-latency path (soft cap or shed), 2) adapt microbatching to prefer slightly higher latency but better throughput consistency.

Sophie: proposal: implement an "adaptive token shedding" policy that:
- applies when queue depth > X or p95 latency > SLO
- prefers soft truncation (drop trailing user tokens) first, fall back to hard max_tokens
- emits a scalar in trace: shed_reason and shed_amount

Matt: +1. we should also avoid immediate kernel switching by adding a small per-device seq-hysteresis: if recent seq distribution had >70% <1024, keep optimized kernel for short tails unless sustained >10s of long seqs. that will avoid flapping.

Linh: we tested a simple soft-truncation experiment: if queue_len>40 and req_len>1200, truncate to 1024, mark response with warning header. result: p99 dropped ~28% and throughput unchanged. tradeoff: a few users see truncated outputs.

Sophie: good. can we add a config flag in runtime config? something like:
```yaml
service.runtime.policies.token_shedding:
  enabled: true
  queue_threshold: 40
  soft_trunc_to: 1024
  hard_max_tokens: 2048
  trace_labels: ["shed_reason","orig_len","trunc_len"]
```

Raj: yes. also add an opt-in per-tenant override (enterprise can disable), and a metric: shed_count, shed_ratio. alert when shed_ratio > 0.5% (so we don't silently chop too much).

Matt: another complementary move: increase microbatch target window from 8ms -> 12ms for endpoints with heavy long-seq distribution. gives a bit more time to accumulate batch without grossly increasing median. we should make window adaptive by p95.

runtime-bot: FYI — created perf-experiment branch: feat/token-shed and a canary job on staging (canary id: cs-20260317-7).

Sophie: awesome. action items:
- Raj: add hysteresis + metrics (shed_count, shed_ratio) — PR by EOD Fri
- Matt: experiment with microbatch window adaptivity on canary and collect p50/p95/p99
- Linh: run token-shedding experiment across 3 device types and report KV-churn delta

Linh: noted. will include a short CSV with sample traces showing kernel_switch_ms vs seq distribution.

Sophie: one more: let's ensure client SDKs surface a non-fatal warning code when we soft-truncate so app devs can surface "response truncated for latency" helpers.

Matt: agree. also add a small doc blurb in the console UI under "Latency protections".

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging/canary -> 2026-03-17T21:30Z (rolling, 3 hosts).

Sophie: thanks all. we'll reconvene after canary runs - if p99 improves and shed_ratio < 1% we'll consider rolling to prod behind a feature flag. :thumbsup:
